newsitem.title: UK: IRA says it shot Northern Irish policewoman.
newsitem.headline: IRA says it shot Northern Irish policewoman.

text.p: The Irish Republican Army on Thursday claimed responsibility for a gun attack which badly wounded a woman police officer in Londonderry, the BBC said.
Security sources said she was thought to have been shot from a passing vehicle while on guard duty at a security hut close to the city's courthouse.
A telephone caller using a recognised codeword contacted a local newspaper in the city and admitted shooting the officer.

Northern Ireland has been in a heightened state of tension over recent months amid growing hostilities by the IRA, fighting to end British rule, and several retaliatory attacks on random Catholic nationalists by pro-British Loyalist guerrillas.
The IRA has killed two soldiers in the province since last October and carried out a series of mortar and gun ambushes.
Late Wednesday guerrillas sprayed two British military posts with gunfire on the border with the Irish republic in County Fermanagh.
